items.title: Single point of failure aur redundancy: ek cheez girne se sab kyun band hota hai
items.one_idea: A single point of failure is any one part with no backup whose failure stops the whole system; find it by asking if this dies does everything stop, remove it with a redundant copy, but failover, detection and cost can become the next weak spot.
items.spoken_hook: एक ही server गिरा, और पूरा app बंद हो गया।
items.hook_formula: relatable_stake: the viewer's own app going dark because one thing broke, plain fact, no question after it
items.visual_idea: One fixed frame: a chain of boxes (user, load balancer, one server, one database) where the server turns red and the app stops; then the server gets a twin and requests reroute to it; last the single load balancer turns red and gets its own twin.
items.everyday_anchor: A shop with one billing counter and one card machine: when it stops, nobody can pay.
items.example: EXAMPLE: one server up 99% of the time. Two such servers, either can serve, are both down only 1% x 1% = 0.01% of the time, about 99.99% (1-(1-X)^N, Wikipedia High availability). Holds only if they fail independently. EXAMPLE numbers, not from a real company.
facts_to_verify: availability of parallel components 1-(1-X)^N and independence (Wikipedia High availability)
